{{short description|German mathematician (1848–1919)}}
[[File:Eugen Netto.jpeg|thumb|Eugen Netto]]
'''Eugen Otto Erwin Netto''' (30 June 1848 &ndash; 13 May 1919) was a [[German people|German]] [[mathematician]]. He was born in [[Halle, Saxony-Anhalt|Halle]] and died in [[Giessen]].<ref>{{cite book
 | last = Sagan | first = Hans
 | doi = 10.1007/978-1-4612-0871-6
 | isbn = 0-387-94265-3
 | mr = 1299533
 | page = 6
 | publisher = Springer-Verlag | location = New York
 | series = Universitext
 | title = Space-filling curves
 | year = 1994| url = https://cds.cern.ch/record/1609380}}</ref><ref>{{MacTutor|id=Netto|title=Eugen Otto Erwin Netto|mode=cs1}}</ref>

[[Netto's theorem]], on the dimension-preserving properties of continuous [[bijection]]s, is named for Netto. Netto published this theorem in 1878, in response to [[Georg Cantor]]'s proof of the existence of discontinuous bijections between the [[unit interval]] and [[unit square]]. His proof was not fully rigorous, but its errors were later repaired.<ref>{{cite journal
 | last = Dauben | first = Joseph W. |author-link=Joseph Dauben
 | doi = 10.1016/0315-0860(75)90066-X
 | journal = Historia Mathematica
 | mr = 476319
 | pages = 273–288
 | title = The invariance of dimension: problems in the early development of set theory and topology
 | volume = 2
 | year = 1975| issue = 3
 | doi-access = free
 }}</ref>
